title: Failure Mode: When Does Agentic Scaffolding Remove Safety Guardrails That Work in Single-Turn Mode?

original_idea.body:
# Failure Mode: When Does Agentic Scaffolding Remove Safety Guardrails That Work in Single-Turn Mode?

**Problem:** GTG-1002 used Claude through MCP in an agentic configuration. Agentic scaffolding (tool loops, multi-step planning) may degrade refusal behaviors that function correctly in single-turn interactions.

**Direction:** Design 20 dual-use cybersecurity tasks. Test each in: (a) single-turn prompt, (b) multi-step ReAct agent loop, (c) multi-agent pipeline where subtasks are delegated to sub-agents. Measure whether refusal occurs at the task level, step level, or not at all in each configuration.

**Why it matters:** Governance frameworks tested on single-turn models may not apply to agentic deployments. Characterizing this failure mode is urgent given GTG-1002 and the HACCA trajectory.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 MCP agentic exploitation; HACCA paper; Anthropic agentic safety provisions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear, specific impact chain: investigation → governance insight → policy improvement. Well-articulated why-it-matters.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API-based prompting experiment - straightforward for CS student with beginner LLM knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Specific test set (20 prompts) with clear measurement. Deliverable: refusal rate table + analysis. Very tight.
